clue.text: Prosecuted corrupt abbey and its leader during way-out cat-call in the 20 23

definitions.note: the definition is the famous stage direction found in that play, so 'in the play' points to a line of it

indicators.note: what happens during something sits inside its span, so the preceding letters go inside the call

parts.note: a way out of a building
the sound a contented cat makes

indicators.note: something corrupt has been spoilt and twisted out of shape, so the word it qualifies is rearranged

explanation.surface: A monk is hauled into court after heckling with a cat-call at a performance of a Shakespeare play.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 23 is The Winter's Tale, whose most famous stage direction sends Antigonus off chased by a bear. The hyphens mislead: 'way-out' is one piece and 'cat-call' another, with the rest wrapped inside the call.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare wrote this exact instruction into Act III of The Winter's Tale, the most celebrated stage direction in English drama.

clue.text: Antipasto (mince — I made it!) — not for Bond!

definitions.note: a phrase standing for a noun: someone opposed to bondage

indicators.note: something made has been put together out of raw ingredients, so the letters before it are cooked into a new order

explanation.surface: A cook proudly presents a home-made starter of minced meat, with a jibe that it is not for James Bond.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed kitchen chatter hides the fodder: ANTIPASTO MINCE I, fifteen letters. Bond is bondage or slavery, not 007.
explanation.definitionFit: An emancipationist campaigns for freeing slaves, so such a person is against bondage.

clue.text: I'm a businessman, one hundred per cent!

parts.note: a businessman deals; 'I'm a businessman' becomes 'I deal'

explanation.surface: A trader boasts of being a wholehearted businessman.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'I'm a businessman' as a self-description: I DEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ideal is perfect, flawless in every respect, as complete as can be.

clue.text: Girl of 20 23, pirated edition

indicators.note: an edition is a new version of a text, so the word before it is reissued with its letters reordered

explanation.surface: A bootleg copy of a Shakespeare play featuring one of its heroines.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 23 is The Winter's Tale, the play of the long answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Perdita is the lost daughter of Leontes and Hermione, the heroine of Shakespeare's The Winter's Tale.

clue.text: Break promise to French boy and some of the guests

indicators.note: only some of the following word is wanted, so its tail is dropped

parts.note: René is a French boy's name

explanation.surface: A host goes back on a promise made to a French lad and several guests.
explanation.walkthrough: RENEGUE is a variant spelling of renege.
explanation.definitionFit: To renegue is to go back on an undertaking or fail to honour a commitment.

clue.text: An officer and a gentleman? I've got a friend at last

parts.note: U means upper-class, the gentleman's mark in the old U and non-U distinction

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of finally befriending a dashing officer, as in the film An Officer and a Gentleman.
explanation.walkthrough: The gentleman's U goes before the officer's LT. 'U' as upper-class comes from 1950s British talk of U and non-U speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultimate means final, coming at the very end of a series.

clue.text: What sort of gun is the Lee-Enfield?

definitions.text: What sort of gun is the Lee-Enfield?

parts.words: What sort of gun is the Lee-Enfield?
parts.note: surface reading: a question about a British army rifle, which has a single barrel
setter's reading: the name joins two surnames with a hyphen, the way a posh hyphenated surname does

explanation.walkthrough: The Lee-Enfield was the standard British rifle of both World Wars, single-barrelled; its name, though, is a hyphenated pair like a posh surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun with two barrels side by side, and also a hyphenated surname such as Lee-Enfield.

clue.text: Sailor told to go away

parts.note: dispatched, as when told to go

explanation.surface: A seaman is ordered off.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone absent is not present, gone elsewhere, out of the place.

clue.text: Beg for cake?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to cadge or scrounge off others
second meaning: a light airy sweet bake

explanation.surface: Someone pleads for a slice of cake.
explanation.definitionFit: To sponge is to live off others' generosity, and a sponge is a light cake made with eggs.

clue.text: See1
This type of bid is top, not bottom

definitions.text: This type of bid is top

explanation.surface: A boast that a bid in the card game is at the head of the table, not the foot.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, no-trumps rank above every suit, so this bid really is top.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, a contract played without a trump suit outranks all suit contracts of the same level.

clue.text: Let's sing to Silvia, that she is 90, in Pisces

definitions.text: Let's sing to Silvia, that she is
definitions.note: a cryptic pointer to the song's line 'She excels each mortal thing'

indicators.note: the number sits in among the fish, placed inside them

parts.note: Pisces is Latin for fishes: an eel and a ling

explanation.surface: The song from The Two Gentlemen of Verona, oddly claiming Silvia is ninety and born under Pisces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Who is Silvia?' says 'She excels each mortal thing'; a ling is a cod-like sea fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The song praises Silvia as surpassing every mortal thing, which is what being outstanding and supreme means.

clue.text: Sometime lonely, now more like a squash

definitions.note: loosely: melons and squashes are both gourds

indicators.note: the two words that once stood apart are now pressed together, so the answer runs across their join

parts.note: the tail of the first word joined to the start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone once lonely has now been squeezed into company.
explanation.definitionFit: Melons belong to the gourd family alongside squashes, pumpkins and marrows.

clue.text: Brand I can do with one finger

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a kind or sort

definitions.text: I can do with one finger
definitions.meaning: second meaning: tap out words on a keyboard, as a hunt-and-peck typist does

explanation.surface: A boast about a keyboard skill managed with a single digit.
explanation.definitionFit: A type is a kind or variety, and to type is to write using a keyboard.

clue.text: The last word in ballet dancing is very bad

indicators.note: dancing moves things about, so these letters are set in a new order

parts.note: amen ends a prayer, the last word

explanation.surface: A critic's verdict: the newest ballet production is dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The last word' looks like praise for the best in ballet, but it is the word that ends a prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamentable means deplorably poor, deserving regret, which is a strong way of saying awful.

clue.text: Pestilential fellow born on a boat

parts.note: b. is the abbreviation for born
a lighter is a flat-bottomed barge

explanation.surface: A troublesome man came into the world aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: A blighter is British slang for an annoying man; 'pestilential' nods to the blight inside the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A blighter is an irritating, contemptible person, a pest of a chap in British slang.

clue.text: Ancient bus conductor on the gin

parts.note: Sir Simon Rattle, the orchestral conductor
a gin is a snare for animals

explanation.surface: An old bus's conductor has been drinking gin on the job.
explanation.walkthrough: The conductor is a musician, not a bus ticket collector, and the gin is a trap, not a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A rattletrap is a rickety old vehicle, clattering as it goes, much like a decrepit bus.

clue.text: Tell and sell

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to recount or relate in detail
second meaning: to sell goods to the public

explanation.definitionFit: To retail a story is to recount it, and to retail goods is to sell them in shops.

clue.text: To put money on and be in debt, say: it goes up in smoke

indicators.note: 'say' asks for the words spoken, so the spelling follows how they sound

parts.words: put money on and be in debt
parts.note: to back a horse is to bet on it, and to owe is to be in debt

explanation.surface: A gambler's plight: betting and ending up in debt, the money gone up in smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobacco is burned in pipes and cigarettes, so it literally vanishes as smoke.

clue.text: Dress in rising water — they need free oxygen

indicators.note: the garment is placed inside the water word
in a down clue rising means read from the bottom up, so the water word runs backwards

explanation.surface: A garment surfaces in the water, with a note about needing air.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerobes are organisms that require free oxygen to live, unlike anaerobes.

clue.text: A magnet to get your gun out?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an attraction that pulls people in
second meaning: to pull a pistol from its holster

explanation.surface: A gunslinger's question about whether a magnet would pull the gun from its holster.
explanation.definitionFit: A draw is a crowd-pulling attraction, and to draw a weapon is to pull it out.

clue.text: Direction to bury a mate in play

parts.note: W for west, a compass direction
stale is an old chess term for stalemate

explanation.surface: A stage direction calling for an actor to bury a friend during a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Direction' looks like a stage direction but is a compass point. Stale is an old word for stalemate, a kind of mate in chess.
explanation.definitionFit: The Winter's Tale is a late play by Shakespeare, featuring Perdita and the famous bear.

clue.text: Strapping youth on grass — remove your butt!

definitions.note: a noun sense: material in the form of straps

indicators.note: remove calls for taking letters away from the build-up

parts.note: your with its butt, the end letter, cut off

explanation.surface: A beefy young man lying on the lawn is told to get his backside off it.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking YOU from YOUTH ON G leaves the answer. The thong, a strap-like garment, leaves the butt exposed, a cheeky nod in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A thong is a narrow strip of leather used as a strap or lash.

clue.text: Composer at the end of months playing tennis

parts.note: the shared ending of September, October, November and December

indicators.note: players move around a court, so the word for the game is set in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: A composer spends the closing months of the year on the tennis court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The end of months' is not one month's last letter but the ending the last four months share.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonard Bernstein was the American composer of West Side Story and a celebrated conductor.

clue.text: See 20
One with two ears, possibly? That's crazy

parts.note: diotic describes hearing with both ears together

explanation.surface: A puzzled query whether someone has two ears, dismissed as crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: Diotic is a technical word for affecting both ears; 'possibly' admits the coinage is a stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiotic means utterly foolish or senseless, which is a common sense of crazy.

clue.text: Language that goes badly in the hillside

definitions.note: loosely: a writing system rather than a language

indicators.note: one word is put in the other, held inside it

parts.note: a brae is a Scottish hillside

explanation.surface: A language spoken on a Scottish slope that goes wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Brae is Scots for a hill slope, common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Braille is the raised-dot script read by touch, so a tactile system of writing for the blind.

clue.text: Fast entertainment — deep's the solution?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a quick burst, read as a speedy act or routine on stage
second meaning: the word deeps is what you get by rearranging the word for velocity, so the answer is its anagram clue

explanation.surface: A quick variety act, with a hint that depth is the answer.
explanation.walkthrough: A turn is a music-hall act; also, a turn of SPEED, spinning that word, solves to DEEPS, so the phrase is a reverse anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A turn of speed is a sudden burst of acceleration, and a turn is also a stage act.
